evidence.scope: Put the harness's security controls where they cannot be skipped: secrets caught before they are committed and again in CI, no environment value able to reach a record, commands allowlisted rather than trusted, evidence passed through files rather than shell arguments, live marketplace hosts refused in test code, and destructive harness operations confirmed twice before they run.
acceptance: A commit containing a fake AWS key is blocked by the pre-commit hook and, when forced through, fails CI: evidenced by a throwaway branch whose failing run is kept and whose branch is deleted
No journal record can contain the value of any variable in the environment at write time: evidenced by a test that sets a secret-shaped variable and asserts every record kind refuses to carry it
The test-code lint fails on api.bol.com, sellingpartnerapi, api.ebay.com, sellerapi.kaufland.com or api.otto.market appearing in a test file: evidenced by the lint and a fixture that trips it

The branch-protection decision is settled and recorded rather than left as a criterion that cannot be met: the free plan refuses it on a private repository, and the enforcement today is the harness refusing delivery and verify-merge refusing a stale receipt
Deleting or rewriting a journal through the harness asks Jev is_destructive, then the human, and records both before acting: evidenced by tests and by the refusal text
CI runs gitleaks and pnpm audit at high, carried in from SEEN-094: evidenced by a green run and by the seeded-secret run that fails

Permissions: .claude/settings.json allowlists the harness commands, the test runners and git, and everything else prompts; the Codex equivalent carries the same list: evidenced by the file and by doctor refusing when it does not parse

Injection: no harness subprocess call runs through a shell, and ticket text, payloads and fetched content are passed as files or as argv elements, never interpolated into a command line: evidenced by a test that scans harness/ for shell=True and for string formatting into subprocess arguments

The recorded-fixture rule is documented where sessions read it, docs/harness/workflow.md, and enforced by the lint rather than by memory: evidenced by the lint failing on a fixture that names a live host
The lint runs in CI and as a qa check, so it is not a thing someone remembers to run: evidenced by the workflow and by this ticket's own qa record
decisions: Branch protection is not bought and the repository stays private: the control is unavailable on this plan, the criterion is amended to say so, and the discipline today is the harness refusing delivery and verify-merge refusing a stale receipt, neither of which GitHub knows about. Founder, 23 September 2026
The environment-value rule is enforced at the one place every record passes through, journal.append, rather than at each caller, because a rule with six call sites has six ways to be forgotten

Only variables whose value is long enough to be a credential are checked, because refusing a record that happens to contain the value of TERM or LANG would make the harness unusable while proving nothing
Destructive operations are refused outright rather than confirmed, unless the confirmation is explicit on the command line: a prompt that a session can answer is not a control on a session
The pre-commit hook is installed by the harness rather than committed into .git, because .git is not in the repository; doctor reports when it is missing
The allowlist names commands rather than patterns that end in a wildcard, because an allowlist that ends in a wildcard is a denylist with extra steps
The injection rule is enforced by a test over the harness's own source rather than by review, because a rule nobody can run is a reminder

A pnpm audit advisory with no fix available refuses the build rather than being waived silently; waiving one is a decision recorded in the ticket that waives it, which is the same stance the harness takes on review findings

The seeded-secret proof uses a documented example AWS key on a throwaway branch, the failing run is kept as evidence and the branch deleted; gitleaks scans the working tree rather than full history, so one old commit cannot fail every future run
graph_impact: journal.append is where every record is written, so the environment rule belongs there
delivery and cli hold the destructive paths that need confirming
